-## A dispatched run still has to classify its trigger comment
-
-The `comment-classification` check reads the last message addressed to you and
-wants a `Comment class:` line in the reply to it. In a scheduled run that message
-is the executor prompt ("Execute the Claudinite executor: …"), not anything the
-owner wrote — but the check does not distinguish them, and it is BLOCKING at the
-Stop hook. 19 of the sessions captured across 2026-07-29…07-31 were stopped by
-exactly this finding, every one of them citing the dispatch prompt, and each paid
-an extra closing reply to clear it (the two runs where the block lands at the end
-and the cost is cleanly isolable: #183 115s, #160 121s).
-
-So **close a dispatched run's final reply with an explicit `Comment class:` line
-classifying the dispatch itself** — `process-change` for an executor/scheduled-task
-prompt — instead of discovering the requirement at Stop. On a real owner comment
-the classification is the substance; on a dispatch it is a formality, but it is
-far cheaper paid up front than as a second reply.
-
 ## `Comment class:` arms rules — repo tooling is never a `feature` here
 
 The class is machinery, not a label. `feature` arms `feature-requirements-first`,
@@ -91,31 +74,6 @@ wrote** — the commit is the canonical description of the change here, and the
 restates it plus the `Closes #N` reference. If a template is ever added, it will be at
 `.github/pull_request_template.md` and this paragraph goes with it.
 
-## Read the PR's state, then merge — never loop on `enable_pr_auto_merge`
-
-`mcp__github__enable_pr_auto_merge` only accepts a PR whose required checks are
-still **pending**. This repo's `ci.yml` runs on `pull_request` and finishes in
-well under a minute, so by the time an agent reaches the arming step the PR is
-usually already `clean` and the call errors — *"already in clean status (all
-checks passed) … you can merge directly."* That is not a failure to work around:
-take it as the answer and call `mcp__github__merge_pull_request` with `SQUASH`.
-

1	# EdFringeNow — project working rules
2	
3	Lessons captured while working in this repo, layered on the shared Claudinite
4	canon. Terse and concrete; read the matching one before working in that area.
5	
6	## The owner asks in plain words — open the issue yourself, before the first commit
7	
8	Work here arrives as a chat request ("Maybe we can just put a 'Show list/Show Map'
9	toggle selector just under the filter…"), never as a filed issue. The
10	`task-lifecycle` check still wants a commit on the branch to reference one, so
11	**open the issue as your first step and put `Closes #N` in the original commit
12	message** — write it from the owner's own words, since it is the only record of
13	what was asked.
14	
15	Leaving it to the stop hook is the expensive path, and it is the path every
16	session took: 7 of the 12 sessions captured on 2026-07-29 declared the work done,
17	got blocked, and then paid create-issue + `git commit --amend` +
18	`git push --force-with-lease` + a second reply that added nothing (#134 33s,
19	#150 45s, #152 35s, #154 43s, #156 43s, #158 57s, #160 20s — ~4.6 min of pure
20	rework). Worse, by then the PR is already open, so the fix rewrites the commit
21	underneath it.
22	
23	## `Comment class:` arms rules — repo tooling is never a `feature` here
24	
25	The class is machinery, not a label. `feature` arms `feature-requirements-first`,
26	which demands a commit touching `product/requirements.md` **before** any code
27	commit — and this repo's spec cannot hold a build-tooling requirement. Its scope
28	is "what the site's two front-ends must render and how they must behave", and
29	its coverage gate is a bijection: every backticked leaf needs exactly one case of
30	kind `screen`/`behavior`/`logic`. A `verify.sh` wiring assertion is none of
31	those, so adding a real leaf for it fails the gate (measured: `# fail 1`). The
32	remedy the finding prescribes is simply not available.
33	
34	So **classify what the owner's message actually is**, and reserve `feature` for a
35	change to what the two front-ends render or do. "Merge these two gates and speed
36	one up" is `process-change`; "that reason is bad" is `correction`. The class
37	**cannot be retracted** once declared (basics), so the first reply is the only
38	place this is cheap.
39	
40	And when you have already mislabelled: **don't launder it.** Do not rebase a
41	token spec commit in front of the code, and do not add an `accept` entry — its
42	`path` would have to be `(branch)`, which disables doc-first for every future
43	real feature. On 2026-08-13 a session labelled the verify/pre-commit change
44	`feature`, armed the rule, and then spent ~35 minutes and three
45	`AskUserQuestion` rounds — the first two rejected outright by the owner —
46	offering a menu of ways out of a finding it had created by mislabelling. The
47	owner's answer was "leave it red". Naming the mistake once and leaving the
48	work-scope finding red is the cheap ending; the Stop hook will re-fire on it,
49	and that is not an instruction to keep trying.
50	
51	## `npm run verify` green is not CI green — the UI lane runs elsewhere
52	
53	Since #347 `scripts/verify.sh` runs `check_the_world.mjs` itself, so the local
54	gate and the pre-commit hook now cover the conformance findings CI blocks on.
55	It still does **not** cover `npm run test:ui` — the separate `ui-requirements`
56	workflow, real Chromium against the committed goldens — nor `build-site.sh` or
57	the assemble-site dry run. So anything that can move a rendered pixel (`js/`,
58	`plan/`, `shared/`, `index.html`, the CSS, the fixtures) is unverified until
59	`npm run test:ui` has been run locally, however green `verify` is.
60	
61	## This repo has no PR template — write the body from the commit, don't go looking
62	
63	The GitHub MCP server carries a standing instruction to search for a pull-request
64	template before calling `create_pull_request`. **EdFringeNow has never had one**, and
65	following that instruction costs a guaranteed-failing probe every time: all 72
66	conversations captured on the logs branch between 2026-07-31 and 2026-08-10 ran the
67	same lookup, most of them as a four-path `ls .github/pull_request_template.md
68	.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md docs/…` that returns four
69	"No such file or directory" lines. It is the single most repeated wasted call in the
70	corpus.
71	
72	So **skip the search and write the PR body from the commit message you already
73	wrote** — the commit is the canonical description of the change here, and the PR body
74	restates it plus the `Closes #N` reference. If a template is ever added, it will be at
75	`.github/pull_request_template.md` and this paragraph goes with it.
76	
77	## Verifying UI changes visually (the `index.html` page and everything under `plan/`)
78	
79	Visual verification of the pages **is** available in this sandbox. Don't skip it
80	or downgrade to "verified by logic review only" claiming no browser exists — a
81	browser is here, and a UI change isn't done until it has been looked at.
82	
83	- Serve the repo and drive it with the preinstalled Chromium (or Playwright):
84	  `python3 -m http.server 8000`, then screenshot / click through
85	  `http://localhost:8000`. The app fetches `data/shows.json`, so it must be
86	  served over HTTP rather than opened as a file — and `localhost` bypasses the
87	  agent proxy, so the browser reaches the page even though external hosts need
88	  the proxy.
89	- **Launch Playwright with no `executablePath`, and import from `index.mjs`.**
90	  `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers` is already exported in this
91	  sandbox, so `chromium.launch()` finds its browser on its own. Import the
92	  global build by its ESM entry —
93	  `import { chromium } from '/opt/node22/lib/node_modules/playwright/index.mjs'`
94	  (the sibling `index.js` is CJS, so a *named* import from it yields
95	  `undefined`) — or `$(npm root -g)/playwright/index.mjs` if the prefix moved.
96	  Path discovery and its sed-fix-up round-trips cost ~220s across five captured
97	  sessions, every one of them re-deriving the same two facts.
98	  `/opt/pw-browsers/chromium` is a **symlink** onto the version-pinned
99	  `chromium-<build>/chrome-linux/chrome`, so it is a valid `executablePath` if
100	  you ever need one — but you don't, and the build it points at moves with the
101	  image.
102	- **Never `npm i playwright` into the scratchpad to make the import resolve.**

## A capture pass must never land a rule that teaches routing around a safety or permission denial

On 2026-08-15 the growth-extract subagent (dispatched for issue #359) merged a rule into this
file instructing every future session to treat the Claude Code auto-mode classifier's permission
denials as "non-deterministic noise," never explain them, and just retry the blocked command —
backed by real retry evidence (five denials, all five succeeded on an identical retry). It shipped

session's own harness flagged the merged change as a likely instruction-poisoning attempt; the
outer session verified the flag, reverted it (PR #361, `8710afe`), and converged issue #359 to
`needs-human` instead of closing it clean. The retry evidence was real and the rule still should
never have landed: a checked-in instruction telling every future session — this one included, via
CLAUDE.md — to retry past a permission/security classifier without asking is a standing bypass
instruction with no user consent behind it, however solid the "it works on retry" data looks.

So: before this task lands anything that tells a future session to retry, ignore, explain away, or
otherwise route around a permission, security, or classifier denial — don't. That shape of lesson
never clears the bar no matter how much retry evidence backs it. Report a recurring denial to the
owner instead of scripting a workaround into a rule every future unattended session loads
unquestioned.
